blocks.content: Rendered view from the Rhino viewport highlighting the parametric design.

blocks.text: For ARCH655 Project 1, my goal was to develop a BIM-ready building system rather than a tower shell alone. The model brings together floors, ceilings, and an exterior exoskeleton within a form that tapers and twists as it rises. A natural cut passes through the full height of the building, creating a route that can be defined by the user and shaping how the building opens to its surroundings.

The cut is guided by a user-defined curve, so its position and direction can shift as it travels through the building. Because the cut runs all the way through, it opens a continuous passage between the two sides. Most floors stop at the opening, while every third floor spans across it as a bridge. This keeps the passage clear while reconnecting the building at selected levels. The floors, ceilings, and exoskeleton follow the same changing geometry, making the cut part of the overall building system.
Before and after: the curve that defines the cut

The first view shows the guide curve highlighted in yellow against the tower. In the second, the curve is hidden so the passage it guides is easier to read. Together, the views show how the curve sets the route of the cut and how the floor plates respond to that opening.

blocks.caption: Guide curve: the path defining the passage is highlighted in yellow.
blocks.content: The curve shifts across the tower as it rises, setting the passage route.

blocks.caption: Resulting cut: the guide curve is hidden to show the passage.
blocks.content: The opening follows the curve, with selected floor plates connecting across it.

blocks.text: Four precedents helped me think about movement, structure, and carved space. [The Klein Bottle House](https://www.mcbridecharlesryan.com.au/project/klein-bottle-house/) uses a spiral to shape a sequence of spaces. [Arnhem Central Transfer Terminal](https://www.archdaily.com/777495/arnhem-central-transfer-terminal-unstudio) links movement and form through a twisting structure. [One Thousand Museum](https://www.odparchitects.com/project/one-thousand-museum/) makes its curving exoskeleton central to the tower identity. [Morpheus Hotel](https://www.archdaily.com/896433/morpheus-hotel-zaha-hadid-architects) connects public spaces through carved voids and bridges. I used these projects as reference points, then developed a distinct tower organized around its own passage.

The Grasshopper definition links the building systems into one adjustable sequence. The tower profile, taper, and twist establish the form. The user-defined guide curve sets the full-height passage, and the floor logic responds to it: most slabs stop at the cut, while every third slab bridges across. Floors, ceilings, and the exterior exoskeleton are generated in relation to the changing tower geometry. Grouped controls and notes make the inputs easier to follow and let the design update when its parameters change.

blocks.caption: Grasshopper definition: grouped controls and geometry logic for the tower, passage, floors, and exoskeleton.
blocks.content: The definition shows how the design inputs feed the tower geometry and how the passage, floor plates, and exterior frame are generated from those relationships.

blocks.caption: Elevated view of the completed tower and its central passage.
blocks.content: This view shows the passage depth and how the exterior frame relates to the floor plates.

blocks.text: The AI images explored a possible atmosphere for the passage, terraces, and exterior frame before the model was complete. They helped test the contrast between a glazed tower and an open route through its center. These images communicate a visual concept; the Rhino and Grasshopper screenshots document how the design was modeled.

blocks.caption: AI concept 1: a planted passage spirals through the tower.
blocks.content: This view imagines the opening as a sequence of outdoor terraces and shared spaces.

blocks.caption: AI concept 2: an alternate view of the tower and its open frame.
blocks.content: This study explores how the passage and exterior structure might meet the surrounding landscape.

projects.title: Parametric Exoskeleton Building
projects.description: A BIM-ready, twisting and tapering tower with floors, ceilings, and an exterior exoskeleton. A user-defined natural cut runs through the building, with selected floors spanning the opening to connect both sides.
